I've written all 8 test statistics to `iter_1/critique/test_stats/`. I haven't run the posterior-predictive check; the pipeline does that. Each statistic avoids ideas already tried in experiment 1 and experiment 2's iteration 0, where all 8 earlier statistics came back non-significant. I checked them only on the observed data and on one random dataset with a 0.36 yes rate: each returns a finite number in about 10 ms, well inside the time limit.

| Statistic | What it probes in `first_example_anchored_reliability` |
|---|---|
| `item_unanimity_rate` | Share of (set, target) items where all answers agree; 40% on the observed data. This tests whether the model's yes-probabilities are too moderate or too confident. |
| `outlier_position_parity_rule_contrast` | In sets where one example has the "wrong" parity, yes rate for targets of the majority parity when that example is shown first minus when it is shown last. This tests the model's own order mechanism directly. |
| `nearest_first_vs_later_example_contrast` | Yes rate for targets close in size to the first example versus close to a later one. It tests whether the first example anchors the size of the concept more (or less) than the model allows. |
| `random_set_inrange_breadth` | Yes rate for targets inside the range of 3–4-example sets that follow no rule. It tests whether people say "anything in range" more than the model predicts. |
| `small_vs_large_far_target_asymmetry` | Yes rate for small (≤15) minus large (≥85) targets far from every example. It tests for a bias towards small numbers. |
| `rule_member_distance_decay` | In sets whose examples share a last digit, yes rate for matching targets far from the examples minus near them. It tests whether rule generalisation weakens with distance. |
| `stray_parity_generalisation` | Yes rate for targets with the odd-one-out example's parity. It tests whether that example widens the concept more than the model expects. |
| `digit_reversal_target_yes` | Yes rate for targets that reverse an example's digits (38 for 83), against comparable targets. The model has no notion of this kind of similarity. |

Each file's `# description:` says which side of the null mean counts as the model under- or over-producing. I also added this iteration's list to the memory note on statistics already tried, so later rounds don't repeat them.
